explanations: formatterFor checks formatterCache but never stores the formatter it creates, so the cache is always empty and every call constructs a new Intl.NumberFormat. Construction is expensive (locale data resolution), and it happens once per line plus once per invoice. A profile of a month-end run shows most time in the NumberFormat constructor. The fix is to formatterCache.set(key, fmt) before returning.

minorUnits returns 0 for JPY, so toMajor divides by 10^0 = 1. lineTotal is 1500 x 2 = 3000, formatted as 3000. Dividing by 100 would apply only to two-decimal currencies, and nothing multiplies by 100.

999 x 825 / 10000 = 82.4175, and Math.round gives 82. It is rounding to nearest, not truncation (the result just happens to match), it would not round up from .4175, and the code does divide by 10,000.

timings.push runs in the finally block, so both successful and failed renders contribute their elapsed time. Failures are not excluded, the batch still returns a real percentile, and no Infinity sentinel is used.
